authoring_notes: Authored against CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0. Primary cards are definition-first and second reveals use the interaction style that best matches the material: compact tables for easily confused governance/risk/agreement terms, sequences for processes, and short action/look-for lists for scenario decisions. Tables are intentionally narrow for mobile use and use progressive row reveals. Glossary entries explain supporting vocabulary rather than hiding the main concept of a card. Current NIST guidance is used where it clarifies governance, risk, supply-chain due diligence, testing, and awareness. Privacy examples use GDPR terminology only where the objective itself names controller/processor and the right to be forgotten; the content explicitly avoids implying those rights or terms apply identically in every jurisdiction. CompTIA's objective body calls MTTR 'mean time to repair' while its acronym list spells MTTR as 'mean time to recover'; the learner-facing card therefore teaches the shared restoration/repair-time concept without forcing one expansion.

User responsibilities and consequences for misuse.

prompts.label: POLICY FAMILY

Data protection and handling requirements.
Incident, continuity, development, and change-management requirements.

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about business continuity, disaster recovery, and incident response?

reveal.text: Business continuity, disaster recovery, and incident response are related but distinct: continuity keeps critical business functions operating, disaster recovery restores technology and services, and incident response handles security incidents.

How do we restore disrupted technology/services?

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about sdlc and change-management policy?

reveal.text: Security governance should set expectations for the software development lifecycle (SDLC) and for controlled changes so security is considered before changes reach production.

prompts.label: CONTROL THE CHANGE
prompts.placeholder: What should policy force teams to do?

items: Define security expectations before development or change.
Review, test, and approve changes using the required process.
Document results and keep traceability after deployment.

prompts.placeholder: What should I know about security standards?

reveal.text: A security standard turns policy into specific mandatory requirements, such as password, access-control, physical-security, or encryption requirements.

prompts.label: SPECIFIC + MANDATORY
prompts.placeholder: What wording points to a standard?

items: A required password length or authenticator setting.
A required encryption algorithm or minimum key strength.
A required access-control or physical-security configuration.

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0

items: Trigger: an event starts the process.
Steps: assigned people perform defined actions.
Evidence: the organization records approvals, actions, and completion.

prompts.label: PLAYBOOK VS POLICY
prompts.placeholder: What is the difference?

Operational sequence
Used while responding

Organization-wide requirements
Explains what is required

prompts.placeholder: What should I know about external governance considerations?

reveal.text: Security governance must account for obligations outside the organization, including regulatory, legal, and industry requirements that can differ across local, regional, national, and global jurisdictions.

prompts.label: ASK WHERE THE RULE COMES FROM

items: Which jurisdictions and regulators apply?

Which organizational systems, data, and business processes are in scope?

prompts.placeholder: What should I know about governance monitoring and revision?

reveal.text: Governance is not a one-time document-writing exercise. Policies, standards, and procedures need monitoring and revision as risks, systems, laws, and business needs change.

prompts.label: GOVERNANCE LOOP
prompts.placeholder: How does governance stay useful?

items: Publish and communicate the requirement.
Monitor whether it is followed and still fits the environment.
Review changes in risk, technology, law, and business needs.

prompts.placeholder: What should I know about governance structures?

prompts.label: WHO DECIDES?
prompts.placeholder: Compare centralized and decentralized governance.

More consistency

columns.title: Decentralized

prompts.placeholder: What should I know about owners, controllers, processors, custodians, and stewards?

reveal.text: Security+ expects you to distinguish accountability from hands-on handling: owners make accountability and protection decisions; custodians/stewards manage or safeguard information; privacy controllers determine purposes and means of processing, while processors act on a controller's behalf.

prompts.label: ROLE CLUES
prompts.placeholder: Which role matches the scenario?

cells.clue: Accountable for the system/data and protection decisions
Determines why and how personal data is processed
Processes personal data on a controller's behalf
Handles, maintains, or safeguards data under assigned responsibilities

items: Identify an asset, process, or objective that matters.
Identify a threat or event and a relevant vulnerability or condition.

reveal.text: Qualitative analysis uses relative labels or rankings such as low, medium, and high. Quantitative analysis uses numeric estimates, often including money, probability, or frequency.

Fast when precise data is unavailable
Useful for prioritization

nodes.title: Single loss expectancy (SLE) and exposure factor

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about single loss expectancy (sle) and exposure factor?

reveal.text: Single loss expectancy (SLE) estimates the loss from one occurrence. A common Security+ calculation is SLE = asset value × exposure factor (EF).

prompts.label: ONE EVENT
prompts.placeholder: How do I read the formula?

cells.meaning: Fraction expected to be lost in one event

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0

nodes.title: Annualized rate of occurrence (ARO) and annualized loss expectancy (ALE)

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about annualized rate of occurrence (aro) and annualized loss expectancy (ale)?

reveal.text: Annualized rate of occurrence (ARO) estimates how often an event occurs per year. Annualized loss expectancy (ALE) estimates yearly loss using ALE = SLE × ARO.

prompts.label: ONE EVENT → ONE YEAR
prompts.placeholder: How do SLE and ARO become ALE?

items: Estimate loss from one event: SLE.
Estimate events per year: ARO.
Multiply SLE × ARO to estimate ALE.
Use the estimate as one input to treatment and cost decisions.

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about probability, likelihood, and impact?

reveal.text: Risk analysis considers how likely an event is and how severe its impact would be. Probability may be numeric; likelihood may also be expressed qualitatively.

prompts.label: RISK NEEDS TWO SIDES
prompts.placeholder: Why isn't impact alone enough?

items: High impact with very low likelihood may be treated differently from high impact with high likelihood.
Likelihood estimates should be based on available evidence and uncertainty.
Impact can include financial, operational, safety, legal, and reputational effects.

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0
NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 — Guide for Conducting Risk Assessments

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about risk register?

reveal.text: A risk register is the working record used to track identified risks, their analysis, ownership, treatment, and status.

prompts.label: WHAT SHOULD BE RECORDED?
prompts.placeholder: What makes a risk register actionable?

items: Risk description and affected objective or asset.
Likelihood, impact, and priority.
Risk owner and treatment decision.
Status, review date, and relevant indicators or thresholds.

nodes.title: KRIs, risk owners, and risk thresholds

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about kris, risk owners, and risk thresholds?

reveal.text: A key risk indicator (KRI) provides a measurable signal about changing exposure. A risk owner is accountable for the risk decision, and a risk threshold is a boundary that can trigger action or escalation.

prompts.label: SIGNAL → OWNER → ACTION
prompts.placeholder: How do these three pieces work together?

items: Measure a KRI that reflects relevant exposure.
Compare it with the defined threshold.
Escalate or act when the threshold is crossed.
The risk owner accepts, changes, or escalates the response.

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0
NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 — Guide for Conducting Risk Assessments

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about risk appetite vs. risk tolerance?

reveal.text: Risk appetite is the broad amount and type of risk an organization is willing to pursue or retain. Risk tolerance is the acceptable variation or limit around a specific objective or activity.

prompts.label: BROAD VS SPECIFIC
prompts.placeholder: How do I tell them apart on the exam?

columns.title: Risk appetite
items: Enterprise-level direction
How much/type of risk the organization is willing to take

columns.title: Risk tolerance
items: More specific limits
How much variation or exposure is acceptable in a context

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0

nodes.title: Expansionary, conservative, and neutral risk appetite

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about expansionary, conservative, and neutral risk appetite?

reveal.text: Security+ describes risk appetite as expansionary, conservative, or neutral. Expansionary accepts more risk for opportunity, conservative favors lower exposure, and neutral aims for a balanced posture.

prompts.label: MATCH THE BUSINESS POSTURE
prompts.placeholder: Which clue maps to each posture?

cells.clue: Willing to accept more uncertainty to pursue growth or opportunity
Prioritizes lower exposure even if opportunity is limited
Balances opportunity and exposure without a strong tilt

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about transfer, accept, avoid, and mitigate?

reveal.text: Four core risk strategies are transfer, accept, avoid, and mitigate. The right choice depends on business objectives, cost, feasibility, and residual risk.

prompts.label: WHAT HAPPENS TO THE RISK?
prompts.placeholder: Map the strategy to the decision.

cells.decision: Shift some financial or operational consequence to another party, such as through insurance or contract
Knowingly retain the risk within authorized limits
Stop the activity that creates the risk
Reduce likelihood or impact with controls

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about exceptions and exemptions?

reveal.text: Exceptions and exemptions are approved departures from a normal requirement. Exact terminology varies by organization, but Security+ expects controlled approval rather than an undocumented bypass.

prompts.label: CONTROLLED DEVIATION
prompts.placeholder: What makes a deviation defensible?

items: Document the requirement that cannot or should not be applied.
Record the business justification, risk, owner, and approval.
Define scope, compensating controls if needed, and review or expiration conditions.

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about risk reporting?

reveal.text: Risk reporting communicates material risk information to people who can make decisions. The format and detail should match the audience.

prompts.label: REPORT FOR A DECISION
prompts.placeholder: What should useful reporting contain?

items: What changed and why it matters.
Likelihood, impact, trend, and uncertainty at an appropriate level.
Current treatment, owner, overdue actions, and decisions required.

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about business impact analysis (bia)?

reveal.text: A business impact analysis (BIA) identifies critical business functions, dependencies, and the consequences of disruption so recovery priorities can be set.

prompts.label: BIA IS NOT THE SAME AS RISK ASSESSMENT
prompts.placeholder: What question does each answer?

columns.title: BIA
items: What is critical?
How does disruption affect the business?
How quickly must we recover?

columns.title: Risk assessment
items: What could happen?
How likely is it?
How should the risk be treated?

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about rto, rpo, mttr, and mtbf?

reveal.text: Recovery metrics describe different aspects of disruption and reliability: recovery time objective (RTO) targets restoration time, recovery point objective (RPO) limits acceptable data loss measured in time, MTTR describes average repair/recovery time, and mean time between failures (MTBF) describes average operating time between failures.

prompts.label: FOUR DIFFERENT CLOCKS
prompts.placeholder: Which metric answers which question?

cells.question: How far back can recoverable data be?
On average, how long does repair/recovery take?
On average, how long does a repairable system run between failures?

glossary.definition: A system intended to be restored after failure rather than permanently discarded.

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about vendor assessment?

reveal.text: Vendor assessment evaluates whether a third party's security posture and dependencies create acceptable risk before and during the relationship.

prompts.label: ASSESS EVIDENCE, NOT PROMISES
prompts.placeholder: What evidence can support a vendor assessment?

items: Authorized penetration-test results or other technical testing.
Evidence of internal audits and independent assessments.
Supply-chain analysis and security documentation.
Questionnaire responses validated against higher-value evidence when risk warrants it.

prompts.placeholder: What should I know about right-to-audit and authorized testing?

reveal.text: A right-to-audit clause preserves the customer's ability to verify agreed controls or compliance. Penetration testing must also be explicitly authorized and scoped.

prompts.label: CONTRACT + VERIFICATION

items: The customer needs contractual access to evidence or an audit.
The vendor must support periodic verification.

nodes.title: Internal audits, independent assessments, and supply-chain analysis

prompts.placeholder: What should I know about internal audits, independent assessments, and supply-chain analysis?

reveal.text: Vendor evidence has different assurance value. Internal audit evidence comes from inside the vendor; independent assessments add external perspective; supply-chain analysis examines dependencies beyond the direct vendor.

prompts.label: LOOK PAST THE FIRST PARTY
prompts.placeholder: How does assurance broaden?

items: Review the vendor's own evidence and internal controls.
Use independent assessment evidence for greater external assurance when needed.
Trace critical subcontractors, components, or suppliers that can create inherited risk.

prompts.placeholder: What should I know about vendor selection and due diligence?

reveal.text: Due diligence is the investigative work used to understand a supplier or product before making or continuing a business decision.

prompts.label: BEFORE YOU SIGN
prompts.placeholder: What should selection include?

items: Define security, privacy, resilience, and compliance requirements.
Research and assess the supplier and relevant products/services.

Document selection, conditions, or required remediation.

prompts.label: PROTECT THE DECISION

items: Disclose the conflict.
Use independent review or recusal when appropriate.
Document the decision process so selection remains defensible.

prompts.placeholder: What should I know about third-party agreement types?

prompts.label: MEASURABLE SERVICE TARGET

items: A measurable target.

Responsibilities, escalation, and consequences when the target is missed.

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about moa vs. mou?

reveal.text: A memorandum of agreement (MOA) and memorandum of understanding (MOU) both document cooperation between parties. Exact legal effect varies, so focus on the authored responsibilities and intent rather than assuming one is always legally binding.

columns.title: MOA

columns.title: MOU

nodes.title: MSA, work order, and statement of work

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about msa, work order, and statement of work?

reveal.text: A master service agreement (MSA) establishes reusable relationship terms, while a work order (WO) or statement of work (SOW) defines a specific engagement, scope, deliverables, schedule, or task.

prompts.label: UMBRELLA → SPECIFIC WORK
prompts.placeholder: How do these documents fit together?

items: MSA: establish common commercial and legal terms once.
SOW or WO: define the specific project or work under those terms.

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about nda and business partners agreement?

reveal.text: A non-disclosure agreement (NDA) protects confidential information shared between parties. A business partners agreement (BPA) defines terms and responsibilities for a broader partner relationship.

columns.title: NDA
items: Protect confidential information
Defines restrictions on disclosure/use

columns.title: BPA
items: Defines business-partner responsibilities

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0

prompts.placeholder: What should I know about vendor monitoring, questionnaires, and rules of engagement?

Monitor performance, risk, incidents, and material changes.

Due care: take reasonable action to protect against known or foreseeable risk.

prompts.placeholder: What should I know about attestation and acknowledgement?

reveal.text: An attestation is a formal assertion that stated conditions or requirements are true. An acknowledgement records that a person received, understood, or accepted a policy, notice, or responsibility.

prompts.label: ASSERTION VS RECEIPT
prompts.placeholder: Which one is the scenario asking for?

columns.title: Attestation
items: Formal assertion about status or compliance
May be made by management or an independent party depending on context

columns.title: Acknowledgement
items: Confirms receipt or understanding
Common for policies, handbooks, or notices

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about compliance monitoring and automation?

reveal.text: Compliance monitoring checks whether obligations remain satisfied over time. It may use internal reviews, external reviews, and automation to collect evidence or detect deviations.

prompts.label: AUTOMATION HELPS; IT DOESN'T GUARANTEE COMPLIANCE
prompts.placeholder: What can automation actually do?

items: Continuously collect configuration or control evidence.
Flag deviations from defined requirements.
Route findings for review and remediation.
Support reporting while human/legal interpretation handles requirements automation cannot decide.

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about privacy obligations across jurisdictions?

reveal.text: Privacy requirements can differ across local, regional, national, and global jurisdictions. The organization must determine which legal obligations apply to its data subjects, processing, locations, and business activities.

prompts.label: LOCATION CAN CHANGE THE RULES
prompts.placeholder: What should a privacy review ask?

items: Where are data subjects located?
Where is data collected, processed, stored, or transferred?
Which entity decides the purpose of processing and which parties act on its behalf?
Which laws, contracts, and sector requirements apply?

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0
EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)

glossary.definition: An identified or identifiable person whose personal data is being processed, using GDPR terminology.

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about data subject, controller, and processor?

reveal.text: Using common privacy terminology, the data subject is the person the personal data relates to, the controller determines purposes and means of processing, and the processor processes data on the controller's behalf.

prompts.label: PERSON → DECIDER → SERVICE
prompts.placeholder: Map each role to the action.

cells.question: Who decides why and how it is processed?
Who processes it for the controller?

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0
EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about data ownership, inventory, and retention?

reveal.text: Privacy and compliance programs need a data inventory: a record of what data exists, who is accountable for it, where it is stored, and how long it should be retained.

prompts.label: KNOW YOUR DATA
prompts.placeholder: What does good data governance track?

items: Inventory the data and processing purpose.
Assign accountable ownership and handling responsibilities.
Apply classification, access, and retention requirements.
Delete, archive, or preserve data according to applicable obligations.

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0
NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — Security and Privacy Controls

nodes.title: Right to be forgotten / right to erasure

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about right to be forgotten / right to erasure?

reveal.text: Security+ includes the right to be forgotten. In laws that provide such a right, a person may request erasure of qualifying personal data, but the right is not universal and legal exceptions can apply.

prompts.label: PRIVACY REQUEST ≠ DELETE EVERYTHING
prompts.placeholder: What should the organization do?

items: Verify the requester and identify applicable law.
Find the relevant personal data and processing context.
Check whether a legal basis or exception requires retention.
Erase qualifying data and document the response where required.

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0
EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about attestation in audits and assessments?

reveal.text: Attestation is a formal assertion or conclusion about defined subject matter. It can be supported by evidence gathered through audits or assessments, but it is not automatically the same thing as an audit.

prompts.label: FORMAL ASSURANCE LANGUAGE
prompts.placeholder: What should be clearly defined?

items: The subject and criteria being evaluated.
Who is making the assertion or conclusion.
The period or point in time covered.
The evidence and scope supporting the statement.

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0
NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — Security and Privacy Controls

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about internal compliance audits and self-assessments?

reveal.text: Internal audits and self-assessments are performed by or for the organization to evaluate compliance, control operation, and readiness before external review.

prompts.label: CLOSE TO THE BUSINESS
prompts.placeholder: What are internal reviews good at?

items: Finding gaps early.
Tracking remediation with control owners.
Preparing evidence for management or external assessments.
Providing frequent feedback, while recognizing lower independence than an external audit.

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about audit committee?

reveal.text: An audit committee provides governance oversight of audit, assurance, risk, and control issues rather than performing day-to-day technical administration.

prompts.label: OVERSIGHT, NOT OPERATIONS
prompts.placeholder: What is the clue?

items: Reviews significant audit findings and remediation.
Supports auditor independence and escalation.
Connects assurance results to governance decisions.

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0

nodes.title: External regulatory reviews and independent audits

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about external regulatory reviews and independent audits?

reveal.text: External reviews may include regulatory examinations, assessments, or independent third-party audits. They provide evidence from outside the team operating the controls.

prompts.label: WHO IS DOING THE REVIEW?
prompts.placeholder: What distinguishes external assurance?

cells.focus: Requirements enforced or examined by an authority
Formal independent audit evidence and conclusions

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about penetration testing?

reveal.text: Penetration testing is an authorized attempt to identify and exploit weaknesses to demonstrate realistic security impact within a defined scope.

prompts.label: AUTHORIZATION FIRST
prompts.placeholder: What must exist before testing?

items: Define objectives and scope.
Obtain explicit authorization and rules of engagement.
Perform approved testing and preserve evidence.
Report findings, impact, and remediation priorities.

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0
NIST SP 800-115 — Technical Guide to Information Security Testing and Assessment

nodes.title: Physical, offensive, defensive, and integrated testing

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about physical, offensive, defensive, and integrated testing?

reveal.text: Security+ distinguishes physical testing from offensive, defensive, and integrated approaches. The labels describe what part of the security program the exercise emphasizes.

prompts.label: WHAT IS BEING EXERCISED?
prompts.placeholder: Match the testing style to its focus.

cells.focus: Offensive and defensive activity coordinated in the same exercise

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0
NIST SP 800-115 — Technical Guide to Information Security Testing and Assessment

nodes.title: Known, partially known, and unknown environments

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about known, partially known, and unknown environments?

reveal.text: Penetration tests can provide the tester with full, partial, or minimal prior knowledge of the environment. Security+ calls these known, partially known, and unknown environments.

prompts.label: HOW MUCH DOES THE TESTER KNOW?
prompts.placeholder: What changes across the three?

cells.knowledge: Substantial internal information, architecture, or credentials
Little or no internal information beyond the target and authorization

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0
NIST SP 800-115 — Technical Guide to Information Security Testing and Assessment

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about passive vs. active reconnaissance?

reveal.text: Passive reconnaissance gathers information without directly probing the target environment, while active reconnaissance interacts with target systems and is more likely to be detected.

prompts.label: NO DIRECT CONTACT VS DIRECT PROBING
prompts.placeholder: Which activity fits each category?

columns.title: Passive reconnaissance
items: Public records
Search engines and public repositories
No intentional direct probe of the target

columns.title: Active reconnaissance
items: Port or service probing
Direct requests to target systems
Higher chance of detection or operational impact

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0
NIST SP 800-115 — Technical Guide to Information Security Testing and Assessment

glossary.definition: Information gathering performed before or during security testing to understand a target and possible attack paths.

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about phishing awareness campaigns?

reveal.text: Phishing campaigns can be used as authorized simulations to teach users how social-engineering attacks look and to measure reporting behavior.

prompts.label: TRAIN THE BEHAVIOR
prompts.placeholder: What should a useful campaign reinforce?

items: Define the behavior to teach, such as reporting suspicious messages.
Run an authorized, realistic simulation.
Give timely education after the exercise.
Measure trends and improve future training.

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0
NIST SP 800-50 Rev. 1 — Building a Cybersecurity and Privacy Learning Program

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about recognizing a phishing attempt?

reveal.text: Phishing uses deceptive messages to push a person toward an unsafe action such as revealing credentials, approving payment, opening malicious content, or visiting a fake site.

prompts.label: PAUSE ON THESE CLUES
prompts.placeholder: What should users inspect?

items: Unexpected urgency, secrecy, or pressure.
Sender, domain, or reply-to inconsistencies.
Unexpected links, attachments, QR codes, or credential prompts.
Requests for money, secrets, MFA approval, or unusual account actions.

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about responding to reported suspicious messages?

reveal.text: When a suspicious message is reported, the security process should preserve useful evidence, determine scope, contain risk when necessary, and warn or protect other users if the campaign is broader.

prompts.label: REPORT → TRIAGE → CONTAIN
prompts.placeholder: What happens after a user reports?

items: Preserve the message and relevant metadata.
Analyze sender, links, attachments, and related telemetry safely.
Search for similar messages or affected users.
Block, remove, reset, or contain as needed.
Feed lessons back into detection and awareness.

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0
NIST SP 800-50 Rev. 1 — Building a Cybersecurity and Privacy Learning Program

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about risky, unexpected, and unintentional behavior?

reveal.text: Anomalous behavior recognition helps people notice risky, unexpected, or unintentional behavior because not every security problem begins with a clearly malicious action.

prompts.label: BEHAVIOR NEEDS CONTEXT
prompts.placeholder: How do the three labels differ?

cells.example: A user bypasses required controls for convenience
An account behaves far outside its normal pattern
A person accidentally sends sensitive data to the wrong recipient

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0
NIST SP 800-50 Rev. 1 — Building a Cybersecurity and Privacy Learning Program

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about policies, handbooks, and situational awareness?

reveal.text: User guidance turns policy into behavior people can apply in real situations. Handbooks provide reference material; situational awareness helps users recognize when context makes an action risky.

prompts.label: MAKE THE SAFE ACTION OBVIOUS
prompts.placeholder: What should guidance do?

items: Use short examples tied to real job situations.
State the safe action and the reporting path.
Explain exceptions without burying users in legal or technical language.

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0
NIST SP 800-50 Rev. 1 — Building a Cybersecurity and Privacy Learning Program

nodes.title: Insider threat, social engineering, and operational security

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about insider threat, social engineering, and operational security?

reveal.text: Training should cover insider-threat indicators, social-engineering pressure, and operational security (OPSEC): protecting sensitive operational details that an adversary could combine or exploit.

prompts.label: PEOPLE + CONTEXT
prompts.placeholder: What behaviors should training reinforce?

items: Verify unusual requests through an independent channel.
Report suspicious insider behavior without conducting your own investigation.
Avoid oversharing schedules, systems, travel, access details, or sensitive operational information.

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0
NIST SP 800-50 Rev. 1 — Building a Cybersecurity and Privacy Learning Program

glossary.definition: Operational security: protecting sensitive operational information and patterns that could help an adversary understand or target an organization.

nodes.title: Passwords, removable media, cables, and remote work

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about passwords, removable media, cables, and remote work?

reveal.text: Awareness training should cover everyday actions that bypass technical controls: password handling, removable media and cables, and security in hybrid or remote work environments.

prompts.label: SMALL ACTIONS, REAL RISK
prompts.placeholder: What should users remember?

cells.safe: Use approved authenticators/password manager practices; never share credentials
Use only trusted, approved devices and accessories
Protect screens, devices, networks, conversations, and physical workspace

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0
NIST SP 800-50 Rev. 1 — Building a Cybersecurity and Privacy Learning Program

nodes.title: Initial and recurring reporting and monitoring

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about initial and recurring reporting and monitoring?

reveal.text: Awareness programs need an initial baseline and recurring measurement so the organization can see whether behavior changes and where more training is needed.

prompts.label: MEASURE A TREND, NOT ONE SCORE
prompts.placeholder: What should monitoring answer?

items: Did users recognize and report the scenario?
Are high-risk behaviors decreasing over time?
Which groups or topics need targeted reinforcement?
Do metrics encourage the desired behavior rather than hiding incidents?

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0
NIST SP 800-50 Rev. 1 — Building a Cybersecurity and Privacy Learning Program

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about awareness program development?

reveal.text: Developing an awareness program starts with business risk, audience needs, and desired behaviors rather than with a generic annual slide deck.

prompts.label: DESIGN FOR BEHAVIOR
prompts.placeholder: What is a good development sequence?

items: Identify risks, audiences, and required behavior.
Choose concise content and realistic scenarios.
Define delivery methods and measurement.
Pilot or review the material before broad execution.

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0
NIST SP 800-50 Rev. 1 — Building a Cybersecurity and Privacy Learning Program

prompts.label: START HERE
prompts.placeholder: What should I know about awareness program execution and improvement?

reveal.text: Execution means delivering the program, supporting reporting paths, measuring results, and revising content as threats, policies, and learner needs change.

prompts.label: RUN → MEASURE → IMPROVE
prompts.placeholder: How does the program stay effective?

items: Deliver initial and role-appropriate learning.
Reinforce it with recurring exercises and communications.
Measure behavior and reporting outcomes.
Adjust content, timing, and scenarios using the evidence.

source_refs.title: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives v6.0
NIST SP 800-50 Rev. 1 — Building a Cybersecurity and Privacy Learning Program
